To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) MI and PE are good statistical measures to detect MWEs, and (2) the size and quality (in terms of control and balance) of corpora are important factors to be considered in MWE extraction, and that (3) the addition of MWEs to linguistic resources improves qualitatively the coverage of such resources.

(1) MWEs can indeed be detected by the statistical properties of their components and (2) the quality of the corpora used for the automatic extraction has a strong impact on the quality of the extracted MWEs.

(a) MI and PE are useful measures to automatically detect MWEs and that (b) web generated corpora can be used as a resource to acquire MWEs, but the quality of the results is highly influenced by the size of the corpus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of methods for MWE acquisition, and their evaluation for grammar engineering.
the evaluation of methods and resources for MWE acquisition and their use for grammar engineering.
the automatic detection of MWEs, their statistical properties, and the impact of the automatic acquisition of MWEs on grammar engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of automatic methods for the extraction of MWEs is a valuable and promising approach for the improvement of existing linguistic resources.
MWEs are not only useful for robust grammar engineering, but also for the development of more general and flexible linguistic resources.
MWEs are best detected by a combination of statistical measures and that the best corpora for this are the Web search engines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while MWEs are difficult to identify, they are also difficult to ignore.
the use of automatically acquired MWEs in grammar engineering is a promising direction, but it needs to be complemented with other resources and approaches.

, while MWEs are a difficult problem for automatic acquisition and processing, it is possible to extract MWE candidates with a reasonable degree of accuracy, and that the results of this extraction can be used to improve existing linguistic resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automatic acquisition and use of MWEs in NLP applications can be done successfully.
, in spite of the lack of control over the quality of web-generated corpora, it is possible to extract useful information for the automatic acquisition and extension of linguistic resources.

, while automatic extraction methods for MWEs are not yet mature enough to replace human annotation, they can provide a valuable support to human linguists in the construction of more robust grammars.
